subject.title: [codex] fix(sessions): report archive cleanup in sessions cleanup

question: Should `sessions cleanup --enforce` now hard-remove eligible `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` archive transcript files using the existing retention policy, and report those counts in dry-run/apply output?
rationale: The implementation is coherent and proven, but it changes operator-visible cleanup of session transcript archives, which repository policy treats as session-state merge risk.

options.title: Accept existing retention semantics
options.body: Merge this after exact-head validation, reusing the existing archive-retention helper and keeping `resetArchiveRetention` as the policy control.

options.title: Require narrower reporting only
options.body: Ask the contributor to report archive candidates without applying the physical cleanup from this command path.

options.title: Pause for broader retention policy
options.body: Hold this PR until maintainers settle how deleted, reset, checkpoint, trajectory, `.bak.*`, and temp artifacts should be handled together.

recommendation.title: Accept existing retention semantics
recommendation.body: Merge this after exact-head validation, reusing the existing archive-retention helper and keeping `resetArchiveRetention` as the policy control.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the cleanup command and disk-budget UX that define the operator-facing behavior this PR changes.
